description: a quarter turn of a revolved profile, a flat from radius 1 to 3 running tangentially into a quarter-round of radius 1 and up a wall to height 2, its end plane's edge along the flat filleted at r 0.1: the edge between the end plane y = 0 and the annulus ends at a tangent vertex, the third edge there the circle where the annulus runs tangentially into the torus, so the chain runs on into the arc between the end plane and the torus — a plane against a torus, a pair with no closed form. Open CASCADE follows the chain and builds it. The chain's second edge, plane against torus, has no closed form, so it is a walked stripe (ADR-0062), and the junction it would meet the flat's stripe in is the ball's arc in the vertex's normal plane x = 3 (plans/nurbs-face-blend step 5b). There the two balls are two: the flat's touches the annulus at (3, r, 0), radius √(9 + r²) from the axis, which is already the torus's, and the torus there lies 1.4e-6 above the plane, so the walked ball rides 1.5e-6 higher, past the junction's tolerance. The annulus turns into the torus along a circle the normal plane crosses, not holds, so no shared arc joins the two: Arris refuses the vertex as VertexBlend, naming both edges and the vertex. The chain walked as one, as Open CASCADE walks it, is a backlog item.
